name: Shin-to-Shin Entry
keyCorrections: If they flatten your shin, your angle is too square — turn your hips to the side.
If you can't enter SLX, their weight is too far back — wait for them to commit forward.
If they grab your head, swim your hand inside and pummel to the inside position.
description: Use the shin-to-shin connection to off-balance the opponent, enter single-leg X (SLX), or wrestle up when they react to the pressure.
shortInstruction: Shin on their shin, off-balance, enter SLX or wrestle up — the shortest path to single-leg X.
summary: Shin-to-shin is the closest open guard entry in no-gi. By placing your shin against their shin and controlling their sleeve or ankle, you create a direct connection that lets you feel every weight shift. When they commit forward, you off-balance and slide your hips under — entering single-leg X. When they back away, you stand and wrestle up. Shin-to-shin is the bridge between seated guard and the leg entanglement system.
whyItWorks: The shin-to-shin connection is the shortest distance between you and their base — you feel their weight instantly.
It requires no grips other than one sleeve or ankle — minimal to set up, maximum return.
The shin-to-shin angle allows you to enter SLX with a single hip movement.
Danaher principle: high-percentage guards are simple — shin-to-shin is the simplest entry to SLX.
commonMistakes: Pushing with the shin instead of receiving their weight — the shin is a sensor, not a pusher.
Letting them grab your head and flatten you — keep your head up and active.
Staying in shin-to-shin too long without transitioning — it is the entry, not the destination.
Forgetting to control the sleeve before entering SLX — without sleeve control, they can post and avoid the sweep.
coachingCues: Shin to shin, feel the weight, flow to SLX.
If they pressure, go SLX. If they back off, stand up.
Sleeve grip is your anchor — don't lose it.
safetySummary: Keep your head up to avoid guillotine counters when they drive forward.
Do not fully extend your legs while entering SLX if they are still standing — knee safety first.
When they back away and you wrestle up, keep your head up to avoid headbutts.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Shin-to-shin connection + sleeve grip → feel their weight → off-balance → enter SLX or wrestle up.

decisionTree.action: If they back away: extend your shin and enter single leg X or X-guard. If they stay close: keep the shin connection and sweep or enter K-guard
Shin-to-shin entries work best against standing opponents. If the opponent is kneeling, consider seated guard entries instead

moneyDetails: Place your shin directly against their shin with your foot flat on the mat — your knee should be at their hip level.
Control one sleeve or ankle with your same-side hand — this is your anchor for the off-balance.
When they commit forward, pull their sleeve across your body while sliding your hips under their leg.
The transition to SLX is: off-balance them forward → release the shin → slide hips under → lock the SLX.
nextStep: After shin-to-shin entry, learn single-leg X basics and single-leg X control to complete the chain.
fixItFast: Shin slipping off? Turn your knee to the side to create a wedge.
They won't commit weight? Circle your shin to create movement and bait their reaction.
They grab your head? Swim your hand inside, grip their triceps, and reset the distance.
